purpose: Define WebRTC as the peer-to-peer transport for DWH/messaging payload channels, with signaling separated from payload transport and all session/channel state tracked as runtime state.

topics.name: WebRTC
topics.purpose: Define WebRTC as the peer-to-peer transport for DWH/messaging payload channels, with signaling separated from payload transport and all session/channel state tracked as runtime state.

semantics.signaling_rule: Signaling/rendezvous exchanges bootstrap/session metadata only; application payloads are not relayed through signaling by default.
semantics.state_rule: Peer/session/channel state is runtime state, not canonical identity.
semantics.identity_rule: Peer semantic identity is separate from transient ICE/session/connection identifiers.
semantics.bound_rule: Session establishment, channels and payload sizes are bounded.
semantics.authority_rule: Successful transport establishment does not grant remote data or operation authority.

invariants.rule: Network identity, transport, remote authority and payload semantics remain explicit and separate.

hard_gates.condition: signaling path used as implicit application payload channel
transient connection id becomes semantic peer identity
WebRTC session grants authority by successful connection
error/timeout leaves runtime session state uncleared

references.purpose: WebRTC is an explicit external/network transport surface.
Transport sessions cleanup on terminal paths.
